title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the central employee-facing guide for working at Redwood. It consolidates the company's approach to roles and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding expectations, and the set of internal tools new and existing employees rely on. Use this page as the canonical reference; more detailed team-level playbooks and role-specific guides are linked in the related pages section.

1) Roles and career ladders

Summary
- Redwood maintains clear IC and Manager career ladders across Engineering, Product, Design, Data, and GTM functions. Ladders focus on impact, scope, technical/functional craft, and leadership.

Career ladder reference table (summary)
| Level | Typical title examples | Focus | Promotion signals |
|-------|------------------------|-------|-------------------|
| L3 | Software Engineer II / Product Manager II | Ownership of a feature area; delivers consistently | Meets goals, reliable delivery, strong peer feedback |
| L4 | Senior Software Engineer / PM | System-level design, mentors others | Leads cross-team projects, measurable impact, influential design reviews |
| L5 | Staff Engineer / Senior PM | Architectural impact, leads major initiatives | Sets technical direction, broad influence, sustained outcomes |
| L6+ | Principal / Dir | Company-level strategy & org effectiveness | Operates at scale, develops leaders, long-term roadmap delivery |

Promotion process (high-level)
1. Candidate prepares promotion packet: role-aligned achievements, impact metrics, feedback.
2. Manager reviews and endorses packet; schedules calibration with People Ops.
3. Panel review with cross-functional reviewers; decision communicated within 10 business days.
4. If approved, HR updates compensation and publishes new role/title.

Promotion criteria (examples)
- Demonstrated impact and scope expansion beyond current role.
- Consistently strong peer and cross-team feedback.
- Ownership of at least one cross-functional initiative with measurable outcomes.

2) Benefits and perks

Core benefits (summary)
- Health: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans (US-based): employer-subsidized premiums, HSA option.
- Financial: 401(k) with company match up to 4%, equity grants on hire and recurring refresh cycles.
- Time off: 25 PTO days (pro-rated), 12 company holidays, generous parental leave (16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary in US).
- Wellness: Monthly wellness stipend, mental health EAP and therapy reimbursement.
- Learning & development: $2,000 annual L&D stipend per employee, internal mentorship programs.

Perks and workplace programs
- Home office stipend for remote-first employees and relocation assistance where applicable.
- Quarterly offsites for functional teams and annual company retreat.
- Commuter benefits for employees in eligible regions.

How to access benefits
1. New hires receive a benefits enrollment email from People Ops on Day 1 with instructions and deadline (typically 30 days).
2. Use the benefits portal (Workday/BenefitsVendor) to enroll; contact people-ops@redwood.com for exceptions.

3) Hiring and onboarding overview

Hiring principles
- Candidate experience is fast, transparent, and respectful. Standard interview loop includes recruiter screen, hiring manager interview, technical or functional assessment, and a final leadership/peer loop.
- Interview feedback must be submitted within 48 hours of the interview.

Pre-boarding checklist (for hiring manager and People Ops)
- Offer accepted and signed.
- Equipment order placed (laptop, monitors, peripherals).
- Badge and building access requested if on-site.
- New hire account provisioning request submitted to IT (Okta/SSO, Slack, email).

First day / week agenda (recommended)
Day 0 (pre-start): Welcome email, IT invite, calendar holds for orientation.
Day 1: Orientation (People Ops), manager 1:1, buddy intro, team lunch.
Week 1: Security training, product orientation sessions, initial small tasks (setup dev environment, read core docs).
30/60/90 plan (template)
- 30 days: Understand codebase/product, complete onboarding tasks, deliver first small contribution.
- 60 days: Take ownership of a bug or feature, present to the team.
- 90 days: Deliver a cross-functional outcome and present results in a team demo.

New hire buddy & manager responsibilities
- Buddy: daily check-ins first week, weekly for first month, help with tool access and social onboarding.
- Manager: weekly 1:1, set clear goals, collect feedback at 30/60/90 days, and complete onboarding checklist in HRIS.

4) Internal tools and access

Canonical toolset
- Identity & SSO: Okta (SSO, MFA enforcement). Owner: IT.
- HRIS and benefits: Workday. Owner: People Ops.
- Communication: Slack (channels by team and product).
- Documentation: Confluence (this space) and company wiki.
- Source control: GitHub Enterprise (repo access via team membership).
- CI/CD: Buildkite and GitHub Actions for specific services.
- Observability: Redwood Console (for product telemetry) and Datadog for infra metrics.

Access request flow
1. New hire account is provisioned automatically via Okta on Day 0.
2. For additional access (production database, restricted consoles), submit a request via the internal access request form linked in People Ops > templates.
3. Requests are reviewed by data-prod-security and approving manager; expect 1-3 business days for standard approvals.

Tooling etiquette and security reminders
- Use MFA for all accounts; never share credentials.
- Tag Slack channels appropriately; use /shh for security-sensitive comms and send to private channels.
- Approve least-privilege access and rotate secrets through the Secrets Manager.

5) Related pages and templates
- New hire checklist (People Ops): /confluence/people-ops/new-hire-checklist
- Promotion packet template: /confluence/people-ops/promotion-packet-template

6) Ownership and review cadence
- Document owner: People Ops (Maya Patel).
- Reviewers: Quarterly review with People Ops, HRBP, and Engineering leadership.
- Review cadence: Annual policy review and ad-hoc updates for major benefits or legal changes.

Contact and escalation
- For immediate onboarding issues: people-ops@redwood.com
- For payroll/benefits: payroll@redwood.com
- For security/access problems: it-security@redwood.com
